title: Mech shared module — Discussions, Datasets and cross-corpus links
Canonical, byte-identical LinkML module shared across the Mech knowledge
bases (CultureMech / MIM / CommunityMech / TraitMech). It carries three
domain-general record sections ported from monarch-initiative/dismech:
* Discussion — the discourse / "knowledge gap" layer. A broad supertype
lifecycle status, hash-anchor `attaches_to` pointers into the importing
* Dataset — a lightweight reference to a public dataset (omics, sequence,
phenotype). Its `dataset_type` / `repository` enums are the faithful UNION
of the existing CultureMech and CommunityMech enums (plus microbial
additions) so the Phase-2 migration of those two repos is loss-preserving.
* CrossCorpusLink — a provenance-bearing link to a record in another Mech.
The importing schema owns the relation vocabulary and which slots admit
links. Sharing a protein or a reaction supplies a curation lead, not an
assertion of record equivalence or biological mechanism.
The module is SELF-CONTAINED: it defines its own `SupportingReference`
evidence class (and `SupportLevelEnum`) rather than referencing each repo's
`EvidenceItem`, so it validates standalone, imposes no per-repo dependency
(MIM has `MappingEvidence`, not `EvidenceItem`), and never collides with an
importing schema's classes. Each record keeps its own primary `EvidenceItem`
for record-level claims; discussions/datasets carry their own lightweight

* species (binomial label) -> ``GTDB:s__...`` via exact NCBI id, else NCBI
species-name fallback (the mapping is strain/genome-keyed, so species ids often
miss on id alone). When GTDB splits one NCBI species into several, report
``f__``/``o__``/...): aggregate the GTDB rank column over the genomes under the
NCBI taxon; ground to the GTDB taxon holding a strict majority (>50%) of them,
report AMBIGUOUS (e.g. NCBI genus Bacillus shatters into ~100 GTDB genera).
Since #372 that aggregation counts only rows naming an actual binomial —
are excluded (#375). It is a real change of denominator, not a tidy-up: it
moved 219 of the KB's stored fractions. An exact 50/50 tie no longer grounds at
all — the name tie-break now only orders the AMBIGUOUS option list (#382) — and
the block records how many genomes the fraction came from (#383).
GTDB frequently reclassifies relative to NCBI (e.g. NCBITaxon "Agrobacterium
deltae" -> GTDB "Agrobacterium leguminum"). ``is_reclassified`` is NOT a flag
for that, despite the name. It is a string comparison, computed at two sites
that do not agree: ``bool(sp and ref and sp != ref)`` on the species path
(which produced 121 of the 154 current true values) and
``top != _clean_label(label)`` on the genus-and-higher path. So it is also true
when NCBI renamed the taxon (NCBI "Allobosea" -> GTDB "Bosea"), when GTDB
dropped a strain designation (Escherichia coli K-12 -> Escherichia coli), when
the difference is a polyphyly suffix (Bacillota -> Bacillota_A), and when GTDB
supplies a placeholder epithet (Dyadobacter sp. -> Dyadobacter sp017744695).
54% of its true values are one of those. See the slot description in the
GTDB CURIE scheme (kg-microbe / Bioregistry): rank prefix + name with spaces as

title: AntibioticMech - Antimicrobial Chemical Structure Schema
LinkML schema for individual chemical structures with antimicrobial activity.
One AntibioticRecord is ONE chemical structure — a compound with a defined
connectivity (InChIKey), not a drug class. "Macrolide antibiotic" is a
structural class and appears as `structural_class` / `parent_compounds` on the
records it covers; erythromycin A is a record.
Records are harmonized from ChEBI (role: antimicrobial agent and its
microbe-targeting sub-roles) and CARD's Antibiotic Resistance Ontology
(ARO antibiotic molecules), and curated incrementally. The mechanism layer —

`causal_graphs` — is what makes this a *Mech* repository rather than a

title: NaturalProductMech - Natural Product Structure Schema
LinkML schema for individual natural product chemical structures.
One NaturalProductRecord is ONE chemical structure — a compound with a defined
connectivity (Standard InChIKey), not a compound class and not a preparation.
"Indole alkaloid" is a classification and appears as `np_pathway` /
`compound_classes` on the records it covers; strychnine is a record. An
extract, fraction, essential oil or herbal preparation is never a record:
activity measured on a mixture is not evidence about any constituent of it.
A compound is admitted by an ASSERTED ORIGIN — a biosynthetic gene cluster, a
cited occurrence in a taxon, or an allow-listed ChEBI specialized-metabolite
role — never by a computed natural-product likeness or a structural
The distinction this schema exists to keep is between `producer_organisms`
(this taxon biosynthesizes the compound, with biosynthesis-grade evidence) and
`occurrences` (this compound was detected in or isolated from this taxon, with
a citation). A compound isolated from a sponge may be made by its bacterial
symbiont. The seeder never promotes one field to the other.
Records are harmonized from MIBiG (producers, gene clusters, cluster class),
ChEBI (identity, structures, specialized-metabolite roles), LOTUS via Wikidata
(cited occurrences) and PubChem (structures), with the filing classification

# Sibling Mech corpora, for cross-corpus links
title: Mech shared module — Discussions, Datasets and cross-corpus links
Canonical, byte-identical LinkML module shared across the Mech knowledge
bases (CultureMech / MIM / CommunityMech / TraitMech). It carries three
domain-general record sections ported from monarch-initiative/dismech:
* Discussion — the discourse / "knowledge gap" layer. A broad supertype
lifecycle status, hash-anchor `attaches_to` pointers into the importing
* Dataset — a lightweight reference to a public dataset (omics, sequence,
phenotype). Its `dataset_type` / `repository` enums are the faithful UNION
of the existing CultureMech and CommunityMech enums (plus microbial
additions) so the Phase-2 migration of those two repos is loss-preserving.
* CrossCorpusLink — a provenance-bearing link to a record in another Mech.
The importing schema owns the relation vocabulary and which slots admit
links. Sharing a protein or a reaction supplies a curation lead, not an
assertion of record equivalence or biological mechanism.
The module is SELF-CONTAINED: it defines its own `SupportingReference`
evidence class (and `SupportLevelEnum`) rather than referencing each repo's
`EvidenceItem`, so it validates standalone, imposes no per-repo dependency
(MIM has `MappingEvidence`, not `EvidenceItem`), and never collides with an
importing schema's classes. Each record keeps its own primary `EvidenceItem`
for record-level claims; discussions/datasets carry their own lightweight
